issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. You may only get a recall letter. The danger shows up if the passenger airbag deploys in a crash.
issues.why: The 9-2X is a Subaru Impreza underneath and uses Takata passenger airbag inflators. Over years of heat and humidity the inflator can burst when it fires and spray metal fragments. Several Subaru-run recalls cover these cars, including 15V-323 (2005), 16V-358, 16V-359 and 17V-016 (2006), and 20V-001, 20V-002 and 20V-003 for cars that had already received a same-design replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls now, even if the car had airbag work before. Don't let anyone ride in the front passenger seat until the recall is done. A Subaru dealer does the repair for free.

issues.t: Front lower control arms can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, a wandering or pulling feel, or in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly tilts or moves back after an arm breaks.
issues.why: In road-salt states the front lower control arms corrode where they bolt to the body and can snap. Recall 11V-464 had dealers inspect the arms and rustproof or replace them. Owners report arms rusting through again years after the recall treatment.
issues.next: If you hear clunks or the steering feels odd, have the front arms inspected right away. Check your VIN for recall 11V-464 at a Subaru dealer. If the recall was done long ago, ask for the arms to be checked again, especially if you live where roads are salted.

issues.t: Raw fuel leak and gas smell in cold weather
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell in or around the car, mostly on cold mornings, and sometimes fuel dripping on top of the engine under the intake manifold.
issues.why: The short rubber fuel hoses and their clamps under the intake manifold shrink and loosen in the cold. Dozens of NHTSA complaints describe this on the 9-2X, and owners have replaced the fuel lines, intake hoses and gaskets to stop it.
issues.next: Fuel leaking near a hot engine is a fire risk. If you smell raw gas, don't keep driving it. Park outside away from buildings and have the fuel lines under the intake inspected before you use the car again.

issues.sym: Coolant or oil seeping where the cylinder heads meet the block, a sweet smell, coolant level dropping, overheating, or white exhaust smoke.
issues.why: Subaru's flat-four engines of this era are known for head gasket leaks, especially the non-turbo 2.5L. The gasket gradually stops sealing after many heat cycles. 9-2X owners report it on non-turbo and turbo cars, mostly past about 85,000 miles.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge closely. If it starts overheating, stop and shut the engine off. Get a cooling-system pressure test; catching it early avoids head damage.

issues.sym: Often no warning. The engine suddenly dies and cranks but won't start. Sometimes a squeal or chirp from the front of the engine first.
issues.why: All 9-2X engines use a rubber timing belt with idler pulleys and are interference designs. If the belt or a pulley fails, valves hit the pistons and the engine can be ruined. Owners report bent valves and new-engine quotes after pulley failures.
issues.next: If you don't have records of a timing belt job, have it done now, along with the idlers, tensioner and water pump.

issues.t: Engine knock from spun rod bearing
issues.sym: A deep knocking from the bottom of the engine that gets faster with RPM, low oil pressure, or the engine seizing.
issues.why: Several turbo 9-2X owners report spun connecting-rod bearings, usually from oil starvation or low oil level. Turbo Subaru engines of this era are sensitive to oil level and quality.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as you hear a knock that follows engine speed. Check the oil level. Driving further usually destroys the engine.

issues.sym: Blue or gray exhaust smoke, rising oil use, a misfire in one cylinder that won't go away, or low compression.
issues.why: The 2006 Aero's 2.5L turbo uses the same EJ255 engine as the WRX. Its cast pistons can crack between the ring grooves after detonation (knock), especially with low-octane fuel or aftermarket tuning.
issues.next: Use premium fuel. If you see smoke or a stubborn misfire, have a compression and leak-down test done before driving it hard.

issues.t: Turbo oil line leaks or smoking turbo
issues.sym: Oil smell, drips near the turbo, blue smoke from the exhaust, or a whistle from the turbo.
issues.why: Owners of 2005 Aero models report leaking turbo oil feed and return lines and worn turbo seals that let oil into the exhaust.
issues.next: Keep an eye on oil level. Have leaks fixed early, since a turbo starved of oil fails quickly.

issues.sym: A burning-oil smell after driving, light smoke from the engine bay, or oil in the spark plug tubes causing misfires.
issues.why: Valve cover gaskets are the most reported repair on the 9-2X. The flat engine puts the covers at the sides, so leaking oil drips right onto the exhaust.
issues.next: This isn't an emergency, but fix it so oil doesn't cook on the exhaust or reach the spark plugs.

issues.sym: Grease slung around the inside of a front wheel, and later a clicking when turning or a vibration on acceleration.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front axles, especially the inner ones, tear and leak grease. It is the second most common repair in TrueDelta's 9-2X survey, and RepairPal also lists it.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot soon. Once dirt gets in, the whole axle usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Power steering pump leak or whine
issues.sym: Whining when turning, especially on cold starts, fluid on the ground, or steering that gets heavy.
issues.why: The power steering pump and its O-rings leak and wear out. Owners report everything from a simple O-ring to a new pump, and one had loose pump bolts shred the belts.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid. If the steering suddenly gets heavy, you can still steer but with more effort; get it inspected soon.

issues.sym: Power steering fluid dripping under the front of the car and a groaning pump.
issues.why: The metal power steering lines corrode in salted-road climates and develop pinhole leaks.
issues.next: Keep fluid topped up and have the lines replaced before the pump runs dry.

issues.sym: Coolant puddles at the front of the car, a sweet smell, and the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic tanks on the radiator crack with age. Radiators are among the most replaced parts on the 9-2X.
issues.next: Don't keep driving if the gauge climbs. A cracked radiator usually needs replacing.

issues.sym: A sudden cloud of steam, coolant spraying, and the temperature gauge rising quickly.
issues.why: Rubber coolant hoses get brittle with age, and owners report upper radiator hoses bursting.
issues.next: If a hose bursts, stop and shut off the engine. Inspect hoses whenever the coolant is serviced.

issues.t: Accessory belt idler or A/C tensioner pulley noise
issues.sym: Chirping, squealing or grinding from the front of the engine; in some cases the A/C belt shreds.
issues.why: The idler and tensioner pulleys on the accessory belts wear out. Owners report replacing them from about 45,000 miles on.
issues.next: Replace a noisy pulley before it seizes and throws the belt.

issues.t: Misfire from ignition coil or plug wires
issues.sym: Check engine light (sometimes flashing), shaking at idle, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: Ignition coils, spark plug wires and plugs wear out. Subaru released improved plug wires for misfires on the Impreza that shares this engine, and oil from leaking valve cover seals can also cause misfires.
issues.next: If the light flashes, drive gently and get it checked. A misfire can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor or catalytic converter
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes such as P0420 or P0031.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors and catalytic converters wear out at higher mileage. Some owners had the converter replaced under the federal emissions warranty.
issues.next: Have the code read. Try a sensor first; ask whether your converter is still under the emissions warranty.

issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattles under the car, or a pipe hanging low.
issues.why: Exhaust mid pipes, flex sections and hangers rust out, sometimes surprisingly early.
issues.next: Get exhaust leaks fixed promptly so fumes don't enter the cabin.

issues.sym: Headlights or running lights go out while driving, bulbs burn out often, or the lights look dim.
issues.why: NHTSA complaints describe lights repeatedly cutting out, and owners report frequent bulb and HID ballast failures and hazy lenses.
issues.next: Check every light before driving at night. Replace bulbs in pairs and have the ballast or wiring checked if they keep failing.

issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the inside of a wheel or under the car, or the brake warning light.
issues.why: Steel brake lines corrode in salted-road areas. One NHTSA complaint describes a leaking line causing loss of pedal at highway speed.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. A sinking pedal is an emergency. Stop driving and have it towed. In rust-belt states, have the lines inspected at every brake job.

issues.sym: Uneven braking, squealing, or pads wearing much faster on one side.
issues.why: Caliper slide pins and brackets corrode and stick, and owners report a sheared retaining pin.
issues.next: Have the pins cleaned and lubricated at each brake job.

issues.sym: A hum or grinding that rises with speed, often from the rear.
issues.why: Rear wheel bearings wear out on several reported cars.
issues.next: Have the noisy bearing replaced before it gets loose.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts clunking
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a bouncy ride, or oil on the strut bodies.
issues.why: Struts, strut mounts and sway bar end links are frequent replacements on these cars.
issues.next: Worn struts lengthen stopping distances. Replace them in pairs.

issues.sym: Grinding into second or third gear, popping out of gear, gear whine, or a leaking input shaft seal.
issues.why: The 9-2X uses the same five-speed manual as the Impreza and WRX, which is known to wear its gears, especially with hard launches. Owners report replacing the gearbox with a used one.
issues.next: Stop hard launches. Have it checked before it locks up or strands you.

issues.sym: Shuddering, harsh or slipping shifts, or fluid leaks in cold weather.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic can shudder and some have failed outright at around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or shudders, get a transmission diagnosis before it fails.

issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, rust bubbling inside the trunk near the strut tops, or a rear strut that seems loose.
issues.why: NHTSA complaints describe the metal around the rear strut mounts rotting badly enough that the suspension could pull away from the body.
issues.next: If you see heavy rust around the rear strut tops, have a body shop inspect it before driving much more. This is a structural safety issue.

issues.sym: The car won't crank or start when you turn the key, or electrical items cut out.
issues.why: RepairPal lists ignition switch failures for the 9-2X.
issues.next: Have the starting circuit tested so the right part gets replaced.

issues.t: Clicking or ratcheting when reversing and turning
issues.sym: A click or ratchet noise when backing up with the wheel turned; sometimes a differential whine.
issues.why: Buyer guides point to low or old differential fluid, and one NHTSA complaint describes a whining differential that needed replacing.
issues.next: Have the front and rear differential fluid checked and changed.
